这个 PR 里没有任何凭据，OAuth client 是我自己在 Google Cloud 建的，client ID 和 secret 也是我自己放进服务器 .env 再重新部署的，在那之前按钮根本不显示，别的也都不受影响

PR 里有 25 个测试，包括伪造、篡改和过期的 state，在另一个浏览器打开回调，发给别的 client 或 issuer 的 token，没验证的邮箱，被停用的账号，昵称冲突，两个首次登录同时进来，还有那个对不上任何输入的密码哈希

title: Fees, intakes and applications on Monash Hub
description: Monash Hub shows 2027 Malaysia fees. A listed fee doesn't mean a degree takes that intake or that applications are open, so each row says not verified.
content:
The fees page on Monash Hub lists what each Monash Malaysia degree costs in 2027, with the change from 2026. Parents read it a lot. The question I kept getting back was some version of “it has a 2027 price, so I can apply for February, right?”

Not necessarily. There are three separate facts here, and Monash publishes them on different pages:


  A fee for a year. The fee tables say what a degree costs in 2027.
  An intake list. The intake pages say which degrees are offered in an intake. For 2027, only the October page has a degree by degree list. February and July only give general deadlines.
  Whether applications are open now. Only a degree’s own page can say this, and most of them don’t say it in words.


The old page blurred the three together. It even had a fixed note claiming one missing degree was closed, with nothing behind it at run time. That note is gone.

What counts as evidence

When I reviewed the sources on 3 November, the Master of Professional Counselling page said in plain words that applications were closed. The intake page still listed future deadlines for postgraduate degrees. A future deadline on a general page doesn’t override a closure on the degree’s own page, so the rules are strict:


  Only a complete sentence on that programme’s own page, about that programme, can produce open, closed or suspended.
  An “Apply now” button, a general deadline table, or a sentence with “may” or “unless” in it produces nothing.
  Two pages that disagree produce conflict, and a person has to look.
  A source that is missing, failed to fetch, needs a login, or was last checked more than 30 days ago produces not verified. The 30 days is my own rule for this page, not an official one.


No model makes any of these calls, and nothing is fetched while you load the page. It reads pages the normal crawler already stored, with their URL, check time and content hash, and shows them under each row.

Matching the right degree

Before a notice can attach to a row, the row has to be the same degree as the page. The fee table links each row to a programme page, and the fetched page title has to match too. On the 8 November review, 62 of 63 titles matched. The one that didn’t was Master of Science against Master of Science (Research). I left it flagged instead of writing a rule that treats them as the same, because they aren’t.

Handbook course codes come only from an explicit Handbook link on the page. If there isn’t one, the code stays empty.

The selection guard

The page has year and intake filters, and they stay in the URL. The API sends back the selection it answered, and the page won’t show an answer for a different selection. Without that, switching from October to February quickly could leave October’s answer on screen under a February label. I had the same bug once on the year comparison page.

Where it stands today

I called the live API while writing this. For October 2027 there are 58 fee rows. 53 link to a programme page, and 52 of those were fetched and matched by title. None of them has an explicit sentence about applications, so all 58 say not verified for the intake.

That looks like an empty result, but there is no reliable source yet. The page still shows the fee, the October list and the general deadlines, each with its own source, and tells you to check the degree page or ask Monash before deciding anything.

What’s still missing

February and July 2027 have no degree list on Monash’s site, so they stay not verified for every degree. The counselling page is the only explicit notice I’ve reviewed so far. Wider coverage is still an open issue in the repo, and the rest of the review notes are in docs/ADMISSIONS-EVIDENCE.md.

title: Monash Hub 的学费、入学批次和申请状态
description: Monash Hub 有马来西亚 2027 年的学费，但有学费不代表这个入学批次招生，也不代表现在能申请，所以每一行都标了未核实
content:
Monash Hub 的学费页列出了马来西亚校区每个学位 2027 年的学费，还有和 2026 年比涨了多少，家长看得很多

我收到最多的问题大概是这样：“它有 2027 年的价格了，那我是不是可以申请 2 月入学？”

不一定，这里其实是三件事，Monash 也是分在不同页面上写的：


  某一年的学费：学费表只说 2027 年读这个学位多少钱
  intake 名单：intake 页面说哪个 intake 开哪些学位，2027 年只有 10 月那页逐个列了学位，2 月和 7 月只写了通用截止日期
  现在能不能申请：只有学位自己的页面能说清楚，而且大部分页面并没有直接写出来


以前的页面把这三件事混在一起，甚至有一句写死的说明，说某个没有学费的学位已经停招，但运行时没有任何来源能支撑这句话，现在已经删掉了

什么才算证据

11 月 3 日我核对来源时，Master of Professional Counselling 的页面明确写着停止接受申请，但 intake 页面上还列着研究生课程以后的截止日期

通用页面上的未来截止日期，不能推翻学位页面自己写的停招，所以规则定得很严：


  只有学位自己页面上一句完整、明确说这个学位的话，才能得出开放、关闭或暂停
  “Apply now” 按钮、通用截止日期表、带“可能”“除非”的句子，都得不出任何结论
  两个页面说法相反就标成冲突，要人来看
  来源缺失、抓取失败、要登录才能看，或者上次核对超过 30 天，就是未核实，30 天是我给这个页面定的规矩，不是官方规定


这些判断都不用模型做，打开页面时也不会临时去抓网页，只读爬虫平时已经存下来的页面，每一行下面都写着来源网址、核对时间和内容哈希

先确认是同一个学位

一条说明要挂到某一行之前，得先确定这一行和那个页面是同一个学位：学费表里每一行链接到一个学位页面，抓下来的页面标题也要对得上

11 月 8 日那次核对，63 个标题里对上了 62 个，没对上的是 Master of Science 和 Master of Science (Research)

我把它留着标记，没有写一条规则把两者当成一样的，因为它们本来就不是同一个学位

Handbook 课程代码也只从页面上明确的 Handbook 链接里读，没有链接就留空

选项和结果要对得上

页面上有年份和 intake 筛选，选择会留在网址里，API 会把它回答的是哪个选择一起返回，对不上的结果页面不显示

不这样做的话，从 10 月快速切到 2 月，屏幕上可能还是 10 月的结果，标签却写着 2 月，年份对比页以前就出过一样的问题

现在的情况

写这篇的时候我直接调了线上 API，2027 年 10 月一共 58 行学费，53 行链接到了学位页面，其中 52 行抓到了而且标题对得上

但没有一个页面明确写申请开没开，所以 58 行的 intake 状态全是未核实

看起来像什么都没查到，但现在确实还没有可靠的来源，页面照样会显示学费、10 月的名单和通用截止日期，各自写着来源，并提醒你做决定前看学位页面或者直接问 Monash

还没做到的

Monash 官网上 2027 年 2 月和 7 月没有逐个学位的名单，所以这两个 intake 对所有学位都是未核实

目前我核对过的明确说明只有 counselling 这一条，覆盖更多学位在仓库里还是一个没关的 issue，其余核对记录在 docs/ADMISSIONS-EVIDENCE.md

title: Comparing a unit across Handbook years
description: Compare requisites, campuses, teaching periods, assessments and exams between two Handbook years. A missing year is shown as unknown.
content:
“Did FIT2102 change for 2027?” sounds like a quick question. Answering it means opening two Handbook pages and reading them line by line: prerequisites, campuses, teaching periods, assessment weights, whether there is an exam. Monash Hub already keeps each Handbook year it loads, so the compare page does that reading for you.

How to use it

Enter a unit code, pick a From year and a To year, and press Compare. Each part of the unit is marked added, removed, changed, unchanged or unavailable, and every result links back to the original Handbook page with the date it was last checked. It is also linked from unit search as “Compare years”.

Optionally add your degree code and the year you started. Your degree’s rules come from the year you started, not the year a unit is taught, so the comparison shows that degree edition next to the unit and links to your course map. Those are two separate things and the page keeps them apart.

A missing year is not a discontinued unit

If Hub has no record of a unit for a year, that can mean the unit stopped running, or that the year hasn’t loaded, or that a fetch failed. The page says it is unavailable and stops there. It never falls back to the nearest year. In a check on 8 November, C2001 had a 2025 edition but returned an explicit 404 for 2024, and the page is required to show 2024 as missing rather than quietly use 2025.

An empty list needs proof

This was the subtle bug. The API always sent a missing collection, like prerequisites, as []. So “this unit has no prerequisites” and “we never read the prerequisites” looked the same, and a comparison could say a prerequisite was removed when it had simply not been loaded.

The parser now stores a small flag for each collection saying whether the source page actually had that section. A comparison only calls an empty list unchanged, added or removed when it has that proof. Old records without the flag stay unknown until the normal Handbook refresh fills it in. The flag doesn’t change a unit’s content hash, so adding it doesn’t look like a policy change or invalidate translations.

Two smaller fixes

Changing the year after a comparison used to relabel the old result with the new years without loading anything. Now an edited form is marked pending until you compare again, overlapping requests are blocked, and a response for the wrong unit or year is thrown away.

What it doesn’t do

It compares one unit between two years. It doesn’t work out whole-degree equivalences, credit transfer or whether you meet a requirement. For those, the page points you to the course map and the official Handbook. The design notes are in HANDBOOK-COMPARISON.md.

title: 对比一门课在不同 Handbook 年份的变化
description: 对比两个 Handbook 年份的先修课、校区、开课学期、考核和考试，缺少的年份显示为未知
content:
“FIT2102 2027 年有没有变？”听起来是个小问题，真要回答得打开两年的 Handbook 页面一行行对：先修课、校区、开课学期、考核比例、有没有考试

Monash Hub 本来就保存了加载过的每一年 Handbook，所以对比页面替你把这件事做了

怎么用

输入课号，选好起始年份和对比年份，点对比就行

结果里每一部分都标着新增、删除、修改、没变或者没有数据，旁边是 Handbook 原文链接和最后核对的日期

课程搜索页上点“比较年份”也能进来

还可以填上学位代码和入学年份

学位要求按你入学那年算，不按这门课开课那年算，所以页面会把你那一版学位要求单独放在旁边，再链到选课规划

缺了某一年不等于停开

Hub 没有某门课某一年的记录，可能是真停开了，也可能是那年还没加载，或者抓取失败了

所以页面只说“没有数据”，不会拿相邻年份来顶替

11 月 8 日核对时，C2001 有 2025 版，2024 版明确返回 404，页面必须把 2024 显示成缺失，不能悄悄换成 2025

空列表要有证据才算空

这是最隐蔽的一个 bug，API 以前把缺失的集合（比如先修课）一律发成 []，于是“这门课没有先修课”和“我们根本没读到先修课”看起来一样，对比时就可能说某个先修课被删了，其实只是没加载到

现在解析器会给每个集合存一个小标记，说明原文页面里到底有没有这一部分

有了这个证据，对比才会说空列表没变、新增或删除

没有标记的旧记录先算未知，等平时的 Handbook 刷新补上

这个标记不计入课程内容的哈希，所以补标记不会被当成政策变化，也不会让翻译失效

两个小修复

以前对比完再改年份，旧结果会直接换上新年份的标签，其实什么都没重新加载

现在改过的表单会标成“待对比”，要重新点对比才算数

同时发出的几个请求会被拦住，课号或年份对不上的结果直接丢掉

它不做的事

它只对比一门课在两年之间的变化，不算整个学位的对应关系、学分转换，也不判断你符不符合要求，这些页面会引导你去选课规划和官方 Handbook

设计说明在 HANDBOOK-COMPARISON.md

title: Study Kit 1.14: attendance login recovery
description: When the attendance login expires, Study Kit tries to sign back in with the browser profile on your computer and stops when a password or MFA is needed.
content:
Study Kit’s optional attendance part reads the Monash attendance portal so the AI can tell you which classes you haven’t checked in to. The weak point was the login. It expired every so often, and the first sign was the AI saying it couldn’t read attendance. Then I had to run monash attendance login again, usually right when I wanted the answer.

Version 1.14 tries to fix that without ever handling a password.

What it does

monash attendance maintain


This checks whether the attendance login still works. If it has expired, it opens the portal quietly with the separate browser profile Study Kit already keeps on your computer for attendance. If Okta still remembers you in that profile, the portal signs you back in and nothing else happens. If Monash asks for a password or MFA, it stops and reports needs_login, and you run monash attendance login yourself.

monash attendance renew --timeout 30 is the same quiet attempt once, by hand.

The rules it follows


  It never types for you. No password, no MFA code. Those stay with you.
  It backs off. After a failed authentication it waits an hour before trying again, so it doesn’t keep poking Okta. Replacing the login state file (for example after you log in again) makes it check straight away.
  It doesn’t mistake a network problem for an expired login. A timeout or a certificate error is reported as what it is.
  It doesn’t lose what worked. If recovery fails, the previous login state is kept rather than overwritten.
  One at a time. Use of the local browser profile is serialized, so two Study Kit processes don’t fight over it.


What it can’t promise

The Okta part of the login only exists on the computer where you signed in. What gets saved for reuse is the attendance portal’s own session, never the identity provider’s. So this works on the same computer, and it can’t stop a login expiring while the computer is asleep or offline. It makes the common case smoother; it isn’t a way around signing in.

Before 1.14, the background job counted a failed keepalive as a success, which hid the problem. It now reports the failure. The changelog has the full list.

title: Study Kit 1.14：考勤登录恢复
description: 考勤登录过期时，Study Kit 会用电脑上已有的浏览器配置登回去，需要密码或 MFA 时就停下
content:
Study Kit 可选的考勤功能会去读 Monash 的考勤门户，AI 才能告诉你哪几节课还没签到

最大的问题是登录：隔一阵就会过期，而且往往是 AI 说“读不到考勤”时才发现，然后得重新跑一次 monash attendance login，偏偏都是赶着要答案的时候

1.14 想在完全不碰密码的前提下把这件事做好一点

它做什么

monash attendance maintain


它会检查考勤登录还能不能用，过期了的话，就用 Study Kit 本来为考勤单独保存在你电脑上的那个浏览器登录状态，悄悄打开门户

如果 Okta 在那个浏览器里还记得你，门户会自己登回去，你什么都不用做

如果 Monash 要你输密码或 MFA，它就停下来报告 needs_login，由你自己运行 monash attendance login

monash attendance renew --timeout 30 是手动试一次同样的静默恢复

它守的规矩


  从不替你输入：密码、MFA 验证码都不碰，留给你自己
  失败了会等：认证失败以后一小时内不再试，免得一直去戳 Okta
换了新的登录状态文件（比如你刚重新登录过）会马上重新检查
  不把网络问题当成登录过期：超时或证书错误就照实报告
  不丢掉能用的东西：恢复失败时保留之前的登录状态，不会覆盖掉
  一次只用一个：本机浏览器登录状态同一时间只给一个进程用，两个 Study Kit 进程不会抢


它保证不了的

登录里 Okta 那部分只存在于你登录的那台电脑上，能复用的只是考勤门户自己的登录状态，Okta 的登录状态从不导出

所以它只在同一台电脑上有效，电脑睡眠或断网时，登录照样可能过期

它让平时的情况顺一点，但不是绕过登录的办法

1.14 之前，后台任务续期失败也会算成成功，问题就被藏起来了，现在会如实报告

完整改动见更新记录

title: Study Kit 1.13: reading your submissions and feedback
description: Study Kit can read what you or your group submitted together with the marking feedback, so your AI app can go through the comments with you.
content:
When marks come back, the feedback sits on one Moodle page and the file I submitted sits on another. To work out where I lost marks I end up with two tabs and a rubric in a third. Study Kit could already show grades, but not what I actually handed in. In 1.13 it can.

How to use it

In your AI app, ask something like:


  Read what I submitted for A1 and go through the marker’s comments with me. Where did I lose marks?


The AI gets your submitted files or online text and the complete feedback for that assignment, then reads them side by side. In a terminal the same thing is:

monash moodle submission <activity id> --json


The activity ID is the number in the assignment list (cmid), not the unit’s ID.

What it reads


  Files you or your group submitted, and online text if the assignment uses it.
  The full marking feedback for that assignment.
  PDFs page by page, and PDF, DOCX and PPTX files inside a zip you submitted.


Video isn’t transcribed, and a scanned PDF still needs OCR before there is any text to read.

Where the files go

Submissions are downloaded with your own Moodle login and kept in a separate data/submissions/ folder. They don’t go into the course library, the full-text index or whole-unit exports, so sharing an export never shares your work.

Every read checks again that you can still see that assignment and that the file belongs to it. Downloads stop at 256 MiB. Cookies are not sent on to another site if Moodle redirects a download. A materials-only profile, the kind used for exporting another account’s course files, can’t read submissions at all.

What it won’t do

It is read-only. It can’t submit, resubmit or change anything on Moodle. It reads feedback on work that has already been marked; it doesn’t attempt quizzes and isn’t meant for answering graded work. The point is understanding comments you already have.

A fix that came right after

In 1.13.1 the assignment list started giving each item a read_path, so an AI that starts from grades can go straight to the submission. That release also keeps a complete cached copy if a later download is cut short, treats a login page in a response as an expired session instead of a file, and reads collapsed online text only inside the submission area. Details are in the changelog.

title: Study Kit 1.13：读取已交作业和评语
description: Study Kit 能读你或你们组交过的作业和完整评语，让 AI 对照着帮你看
content:
成绩出来以后，评语在 Moodle 的一个页面，自己交的文件在另一个页面，想弄清楚哪里扣分，得开两个标签页，再加一个评分标准

Study Kit 以前能看成绩，但看不到我到底交了什么，1.13 开始可以了

怎么用

在 AI 里这样问：


  把我 A1 交的东西读一遍，对照老师的评语，具体说说哪里扣分


AI 会拿到你交的文件或在线文本，以及这份作业的完整反馈，放在一起看，终端里对应的是：

monash moodle submission <activity id> --json


activity id 用作业列表里的那个编号（cmid），不是课程 ID

它读什么


  你或你们组交的文件，作业用在线文本的话也会读
  这份作业完整的评分反馈
  PDF 可以按页读；你交的压缩包里的 PDF、DOCX、PPTX 也能读


视频不会自动转成文字，扫描版的 PDF 要先 OCR 才有字可读

文件存在哪

交过的作业用你自己的 Moodle 登录下载，单独放在 data/submissions/ 里，不进课件库、全文索引和整课导出，所以把导出的资料发给别人时，不会把你的作业一起发出去

每次读都会重新确认你还能看到这份作业、这个文件确实属于它，下载上限 256 MiB，Moodle 跳转下载时，cookie 不会跟着发到别的网站，只导课程资料的账号（用来导另一个账号课件的那种）完全读不了这些

它不做的事

它只读，不能交作业、重交，也不会改 Moodle 上的任何东西

它读的是已经批改完的作业的反馈，不做测验，也不是拿来答需要评分的作业的，只是帮你看懂已经拿到的评语

紧接着的一个修复

1.13.1 让作业列表里每一项都带上 read_path，AI 从成绩开始问的话，可以直接接着读交过的文件

这一版还修了几处：后面的下载被截断时保留之前完整的缓存；返回的是登录页时当作登录过期，不当成文件；折叠起来的在线文本只在提交区域里读

详细见更新记录

title: Study Kit 1.12: monash changes
description: A local log of new files, edited assignment instructions, moved deadlines and staff replies in your units.
content:
Every week someone in a group chat asks whether the A2 deadline moved or whether the lecturer changed the spec. Moodle doesn’t tell you. You have to remember what it said last week and compare. Study Kit already syncs a copy of each unit to my laptop, so in 1.12 I made it remember what it saw and tell me what is different.

What it shows

monash changes --days 7


It lists new or edited course files, assignment instructions that were rewritten, deadline times that moved (with the old and new time), and new staff replies on Ed. Each line has the unit, what kind of change it is, and a link back to the original. The same list shows up when I ask my AI “what changed this week?”, and inside study todo.

How it works

All of it lives in changes.py and one local SQLite file, changes.db. During a normal sync, each item gets a fingerprint. Course files, Ed lesson files and saved assignment instructions get a SHA-256 of the file. Deadlines are compared by their due time. Staff posts and replies on Ed get a SHA-256 of their text. The next sync compares fingerprints. Nothing extra is fetched from Moodle or Ed for this; it only looks at what the sync already downloaded.

Hashing every PDF on every sync would be slow, so for files it keeps the path, modified time and size next to the hash. If those three haven’t changed, it reuses the old hash.

Three rules I care about

The first sync is only a baseline. The first time it sees a unit, it records everything and reports nothing. Otherwise a new install would announce that every file in the unit is “new”.

It never reports something as removed. If an item is missing from one sync, that could be a real removal, or a page that timed out halfway. I can’t tell the two apart reliably, so the log only records additions and changes. A false “the brief was deleted” is worse than saying nothing.

It forgets. Entries older than 90 days are dropped, and the table keeps at most 5,000 rows.

The part that made it worth doing

The change log is only useful if syncs are reliable, so most of 1.12 is actually about that. A Moodle outage or rate limit used to look the same as an expired login. Now they are told apart, safe reads retry with backoff, and a sync that only half worked says so instead of reporting success. monash sync --retry-failed retries just the activities, posts and Lessons that failed last time, rather than the whole semester.

The changelog for 1.12.0 lists the rest, including Australian timezones with daylight saving (monash config timezone Australia/Melbourne).

title: Study Kit 1.12：monash changes
description: 在本机记录课程里新上的文件、改过的作业说明、调整的截止时间和老师的新回复
content:
每周群里都有人问：A2 是不是延期了？老师是不是改了 spec？Moodle 不会告诉你，只能靠自己记得上周写的是什么再对一遍

Study Kit 本来就会把每门课同步一份到我电脑上，所以 1.12 里我让它记住上次看到的东西，再告诉我哪里不一样了

它显示什么

monash changes --days 7


会列出新上传或改过的课件、被重写的作业说明、挪过的截止时间（新旧时间都写出来），还有 Ed 上老师的新回复，每一条都有课号、改动类型和原文链接

在 AI 里问“这周我的课有什么变化”，或者看 study todo，也是同一份列表

怎么做的

全部在 changes.py 和本机的一个 SQLite 文件 changes.db 里

平时同步的时候，每一项都会算一个指纹：课件、Ed 里的文件和存下来的作业说明，算的是文件的 SHA-256；截止时间直接比时间；Ed 上老师的帖子和回复，算的是正文的 SHA-256，下次同步再比指纹

这个功能不会为了比较多请求一次 Moodle 或 Ed，只看同步本来就下载下来的东西

每次同步都把所有 PDF 重新算一遍哈希太慢了，所以文件会在哈希旁边记下路径、修改时间和大小，这三样都没变就直接用旧的哈希

我比较在意的三条规则

第一次同步只建基线：第一次看到某门课时，只把所有东西记下来，什么都不报

不然刚装好就会说这门课的每个文件都是“新的”

从不报“被删除”：某次同步里少了一项，可能真是被删了，也可能是页面加载到一半超时了

这两种情况分不清，所以记录里只有新增和修改，错报一句“作业说明被删了”比什么都不说更糟

会忘记：超过 90 天的记录会删掉，最多只留 5000 条

花时间最多的部分

变更记录要靠得住，前提是同步本身靠得住，所以 1.12 大部分改动其实在这上面

以前 Moodle 宕机或者限流，看起来和登录过期一模一样，现在能分开了

安全的读取会隔一会儿再试，只成功一半的同步会照实说出来，不再报成功

monash sync --retry-failed 只重试上次失败的活动、帖子和 Lessons，不用整个学期重新拉一遍

其他改动见 1.12.0 的更新记录，包括带夏令时的澳洲时区（monash config timezone Australia/Melbourne）

title: Finding electives on Monash Hub
description: Filter free electives by exam, prerequisites and campus. There is no final exam filter because the data can't support it.
content:
Choosing a free elective comes down to three questions that I get asked every semester: does it have an exam, does it need a prerequisite, and is it taught at my campus. Monash Hub could already filter the unit list on all three, but nobody finds a filter they do not know exists. So there is now a page for electives that links straight into the list with those filters set.

What the page does

There are four conditions at the top: no exam listed, no prerequisite listed, both together, and level 1 units with no prerequisite listed. Each shows how many units fit. Pick one and the page lists 12 undergraduate units that fit, with a button to the full unit list with the filters already set. A campus switch (Malaysia or Australia) follows the same cookie as the home page.

The 12 units take turns between faculties. In code order the first dozen were all accounting units starting with ACB or ACM, so the API got a sort=mixed option: the lowest-level unit of each faculty first, then the next of each. The first version also had a list grouped by faculty. I removed it, because the Handbook’s faculty field mixes faculties with departments and the list looked messy.

The page never says a unit is easy and never recommends one. Whether a unit counts as a free elective depends on the course, so the page says to check the course page or the progression map, and ask the faculty when unsure.

What “no prerequisite” means

The no_prereq filter keeps the units that have no prerequisite group in the Handbook data. It means the Handbook lists none. An entry requirement written only in the unit’s description text is not a prerequisite group, so it can still exist. The page says this next to the filter, because “not listed” is not the same as “none”.

Why there is no final exam filter

Students often ask for units with no final exam, and I wanted to add that filter. Then I looked at the data. The exam filter works from assessment names that contain “exam” or “examination”. In a sample of 120 live units I found 55 such items. Only 3 were named final and 1 was named mid. The other 51 were just called “Examination”.

So the Handbook data cannot tell a final exam from a midterm, and a filter that claimed to would be guessing. I kept one filter, “no exam listed”, and the page says that final and midterm exams both count as exams, while quizzes and tests do not. A student who wants to avoid a final still needs to open the unit and read the assessment table.

I also got this wrong once. My first wording on the page and in the bot said units with “no final exam”, which the filter does not know. I changed it to “no exam listed” in #291.

How the bot sends people there

In qa/hub-topics.json there are four answers for the bot. When someone asks about electives, units without an exam, units without a prerequisite, or what is taught in a semester, it replies with the electives page and the unit list link with the filter set, for the Malaysia campus, plus a line on how to switch campus. If someone asks for “no final exam”, the answer says one filter exists, for no exam listed, and explains what that covers. The answers have to be imported on the server before the bot uses them.

title: 在 Monash Hub 上找选修课
description: 按考试、先修课和校区筛选选修课，没有“期末考试”筛选是因为数据不够可靠
content:
挑自由选修课时，每学期都有人问我同样三件事：有没有考试，要不要先修课，自己的校区开不开

Monash Hub 的课程列表本来就能按这三项筛选，但不知道有筛选的人是不会去找的

所以现在加了一个选修课页面，点进去就是已经筛好的课程列表

页面做什么

页面顶部有四个条件：没列出考试、没列出先修课、两个都没列出，以及一年级且没列出先修课的课，每个都显示有多少门课符合

选一个，下面就列出 12 门符合的本科课，再给一个按钮进到已经设好筛选的完整课程列表

校区可以切换（马来西亚或澳大利亚），和首页用的是同一个 cookie

这 12 门课会轮流取各个学院的

按课程代码排的话，前 12 门全是 ACB、ACM 开头的会计课，所以我给接口加了 sort=mixed：先取每个学院等级最低的一门，再取每个学院的下一门

第一版还有一份按学院分组的列表，后来删了，因为 Handbook 里的“学院”字段混着学院和系，看起来很乱

页面不会说哪门课好过，也不推荐任何一门

一门课算不算自由选修课要看你的专业，所以页面提醒去看专业页面或课程规划图，拿不准就问学院

“没有先修课”是什么意思

no_prereq 筛选留下的是 Handbook 数据里没有先修课条件的课

意思是 Handbook 没列出

只写在课程介绍文字里的入学要求不算先修课条件，所以可能仍然存在

页面在筛选旁边写明了这一点，因为“没列出”和“没有”不是一回事

为什么没有“期末考试”筛选

经常有人问有没有没期末考试的课，我本来想加这个筛选

后来看了数据

考试筛选依据的是评估项名称里带 exam 或 examination 的条目

我抽了 120 门在线课程，一共找到 55 个这样的条目，只有 3 个名字里写了 final，1 个写了 mid，剩下 51 个就叫 “Examination”

也就是说 Handbook 数据分不出期末考试和期中考试，一个声称能分的筛选只是在猜

所以我只保留了“没列出考试”这一个，页面写明期末和期中都算考试，小测验不算

想避开期末考试的同学，还是得点进课程看评估表

这件事我之前也说错过

页面和机器人最初的说法是“没有期末考试”，但筛选根本不认识这个概念

我在 #291 里改成了“没列出考试”

机器人怎么带人过来

机器人在 qa/hub-topics.json 里有四条回答

有人问选修课、没考试的课、没先修课的课，或者某学期开什么课时，它会回复选修课页面和已经设好筛选的课程列表链接（马来西亚校区），再加一句怎么切换校区

问到“没有期末考试”时，回答会说只有一个“没列出考试”的筛选，并解释它包含什么

这些回答要在服务器上导入之后，机器人才会用

title: Teaching the bot with normal messages
description: The bot now treats my plain messages as knowledge and tells a new fact from a correction or an answer, and asks when it isn't sure.
content:
Teaching the bot used to need a format: 答 12 … to answer a waiting question, 教 问题 | 答案 to add a Q&A. I knew the answers, but typing the format each time felt like a chore, so often I did not reply at all and the same question came back the next week. On 17 November I changed it so a plain message from me is read as knowledge.

Reading the shape of the message

There is no language model in this part. wxbot/teach.py looks at the shape of the line and picks the first case that fits:


  A question mark with text after it: 学生证丢了怎么办？去 Student Services 补办. The part before is the question, the part after is the answer.
  A first line followed by more lines: the first line is the question, the rest is the answer.
  A short label and a colon: 驾校：马莫百科不推荐，自己查.
  One full statement. Its first clause becomes the phrasing, and the bot tells me that it guessed, so I can send a better phrasing later.


A question with nothing after it is not knowledge. If I send “学费怎么交”, I am trying the bot, so it just answers. A line shorter than 8 characters is also not taken as a fact. If I do want a line stored that reads like a question, 记 一句话 forces it.

Not guessing when it matters

What the bot stores is visible to students, so I made it ask when it is unsure instead of choosing.

If a pair about the same thing already exists, the bot replies with one digit to choose: 1 replaces the old answer, 2 adds to it, 3 stores a new pair, 0 stores nothing. If my line repeats a waiting question and says more than the question did, it is sent to that asker as the answer. If my line is very short, like “可以”, the bot asks which waiting question it belongs to. Nothing goes to a student on a guess about that.

Every automatic change can be undone with 撤销, which removes the last pair the bot stored or changed. It only covers that one, so a mistake from three messages ago is fixed by hand.

Skipping many at once

Before, a waiting question had to be ignored one at a time. Now 忽略 12 13 14, 忽略 12-20 and 忽略 全部 all work, with no limit on how many. Quoting a note and replying 跳过 skips that one. I added this because after a busy week there were more notes than I wanted to touch individually.

What is still manual

The bot cannot tell that an answer from me is out of date. If the visa rules change, I have to say so, and the old pair stays until I do. The 1, 2, 3 choice is also the part I trust least. I will watch whether I keep picking the same digit, because then it should be the default.

title: 用平常的消息教机器人
description: 现在我平常发的消息会被当成知识，机器人会区分新知识、更正和回答，不确定时会先问我
content:
以前教机器人要用固定格式：回答待答用 答 12 …，新增问答用 教 问题 | 答案

答案我是知道的，但每次都要打格式，觉得麻烦，所以经常干脆不回，同一个问题下周又来了

11 月 17 日我改成了：我发的普通消息会被当成知识

看消息的样子

这一部分没有用大模型

wxbot/teach.py 看一句话长什么样，按顺序找第一个符合的情况：


  问号后面还有字：学生证丢了怎么办？去 Student Services 补办，前面是问题，后面是答案
  第一行后面还有几行：第一行是问题，剩下的是答案
  短标题加冒号：驾校：马莫百科不推荐，自己查
  一句完整的陈述，它的第一个分句当作问法，机器人会告诉我这是它猜的，我可以之后再发更好的问法


只有问题、后面什么都没有的不算知识

我发“学费怎么交”，是在试机器人，它就直接回答

短于 8 个字的一句话也不会被当成事实

如果我确实想存一句看起来像提问的话，用 记 一句话 强制记下

重要的地方不靠猜

机器人记下的内容学生看得到，所以我让它拿不准时先问我，不自己选

已有关于同一件事的问答时，机器人回一个数字让我选：1 换掉旧答案，2 接在后面，3 另存一条，0 不记

我发的话重复了某条待答、并且比问题说得更多，就直接作为答案发给那个提问的人

我发的话很短，比如“可以”，机器人会先问这是回答哪一条待答

凡是涉及发给学生的内容，都不会靠猜

自动改的东西都可以用 撤销 收回，它会删掉机器人刚记下或改过的最后一条

只能撤这一条，三条消息之前的错误还是要手动改

一次忽略很多条

以前待答只能一条一条忽略

现在 忽略 12 13 14、忽略 12-20、忽略 全部 都可以，数量没有上限

引用某条通知回复 跳过 也行

加这个是因为忙过一周之后，待答多到我不想一条条点

还要手动的部分

机器人看不出我之前的回答已经过期

签证规则变了，我得自己说一声，在我说之前旧的那条会一直在

1、2、3 的选择也是我最没把握的一块

我会留意自己是不是总选同一个数字，如果是，就该把它设成默认

title: Which messages the bot forwards to me
description: The bot used to forward every message it couldn't answer. Now it filters small talk and noise and has a daily cap per person.
content:
The 马莫百科 bot forwards a question to me when it cannot answer it. For a while that also meant “哈哈哈你好可爱”, “怎么办”, “asdfgh”, adverts, and sometimes swearing. Every one of them became a pending note in my admin chat, and I had to read it and decide it was nothing. On 16 November I decided those should not reach me at all.

Two checks instead of one

The obvious fix is one filter in front of everything. I did not want that, because the knowledge base should still get the first try at anything that might be a question. So there are two checks, in wxbot/triage.py.

The first runs before the knowledge base. It catches noise, swearing, small talk, adverts, “有人吗” and requests to do graded work. Running it first matters for a practical reason: a loose match can turn “哈哈哈” into “你问的是不是…” about some unrelated Q&A, which is worse than no answer.

The second runs only after nothing could answer. It catches a message that is too short to act on (“怎么办”), a request for a general chatbot (“帮我翻译一下”), and a remark that has no question in it and nothing about study. The asker gets a short reply that says what kind of message the bot can use, with two examples such as “FIT2102 有期末考试吗”. Adverts get no reply.

When in doubt, forward

Holding back a real question costs more than receiving a pointless one. So every rule leans towards letting the message through. A message is held only when it clearly matches one of the cases above. Anyone who is held can reply 「人工」 and it is forwarded anyway.

A cap per person

One person sending question after question would still fill my chat, even if every question is real. Each person can now have 5 forwarded questions in 24 hours. After that the bot says how many it has already passed on and points to Monash Hub. The number is WXBOT_PENDING_DAILY, and 0 turns the cap off. WXBOT_SCREEN=0 turns the whole triage off if it ever misbehaves.

How I tested it

tests/test_triage.py has two lists. 41 messages students and parents might send must be forwarded, such as “没回国能线上报到吗”, “我 offer 丢了” and “怎么扔垃圾”. 39 messages must be held, such as greetings, keyboard mashing and requests like “帮我写 assignment”. If a change breaks either list, the tests fail.

I also wrote 114 questions that students and parents ask into eval/common-questions.txt. python -m wxbot coverage asks the bot every one of them and lists the ones it cannot answer. That list is what I add Q&As from now.

What I do not know yet

I could not read the server’s real message log while writing this, so both lists are samples I wrote from what I remember being asked. The rules are tuned to those, not to what people really send. After a week of use I will look at what was held and check that nothing real was in it. The counts and the cap are the first thing I will change if it was wrong.

title: 机器人哪些消息转给我
description: 机器人以前把答不上来的消息全转给我，现在会过滤闲聊和乱码，每人每天也有上限
content:
马莫百科机器人答不上来的问题会转给我

之前这也包括“哈哈哈你好可爱”“怎么办”“asdfgh”、广告，偶尔还有骂人的话

每一条都会在我的管理员聊天里变成一条待答，我得点开看，再确认它什么都不是

11 月 16 日我决定，这些不应该再到我这里

两道检查，不是一道

最直接的做法是在最前面加一个过滤

我没这么做，因为知识库应该先试一遍所有可能是问题的消息

所以分成两道，写在 wxbot/triage.py 里

第一道在知识库之前

它挡住乱码、骂人、闲聊、广告、“有人吗”，还有让机器人帮忙做作业的请求

放在前面有实际原因：模糊匹配会把“哈哈哈”变成对某条无关问答的“你问的是不是…”，这比不回答更糟

第二道只在什么都答不上之后才看

它挡住短到没法处理的消息（“怎么办”）、把机器人当通用聊天助手的请求（“帮我翻译一下”），以及既没有问题也和学习无关的一句话

提问的人会收到一句简短的回复，说明机器人能处理什么样的话，并给两个例子，比如“FIT2102 有期末考试吗”

广告不回复

拿不准就转

拦掉一个真问题的代价，比多收一句废话大得多

所以每条规则都偏向放行，只有明确属于上面几类才会被拦

被拦的人回复「人工」，照样会转给我

每人每天有上限

就算每个问题都是真的，一个人连着发也会把我的聊天塞满

现在每人 24 小时内最多转 5 个问题，超过之后机器人会告诉他已经转了几个，并指向 Monash Hub

这个数字是 WXBOT_PENDING_DAILY，设为 0 就取消上限

WXBOT_SCREEN=0 可以把整个分流关掉，万一出问题可以马上退回去

怎么测的

tests/test_triage.py 里有两份清单

41 条同学和家长可能发的话必须转发，比如“没回国能线上报到吗”“我 offer 丢了”“怎么扔垃圾”

39 条必须拦住，比如问候、乱按键盘，还有“帮我写 assignment”这类请求

改动让任何一份清单出错，测试就会失败

我还把 114 个同学和家长会问的问题写进了 eval/common-questions.txt

python -m wxbot coverage 会把它们挨个问一遍机器人，列出答不上来的

以后补问答就照这份列表来

我还不知道的

写这些的时候我没法读服务器上的真实消息记录，所以两份清单都是我凭印象写的样本，规则是按它们调的，不是按大家真正发的话

用一个星期后，我会翻一遍被拦下的消息，确认里面没有真问题

如果拦错了，先改的是数字和上限

title: Exporting a whole unit's course materials
description: Study Kit 1.8 to 1.11.1 export Moodle pages, Books, assignment briefs, Ed Lessons and linked Google files as one local package with a list of what is missing.
content:
The earlier Ed export article covered lesson folders and a download-all zip. A course has more than Ed files: a Moodle Page containing the brief, a Book with several chapters, a marking guide, pictures embedded in a lesson, and a Google document that is still only a link. Packing the PDFs already on disk leaves all of those behind.

Study Kit 1.8 added a whole-course package. Versions 1.9 through 1.11.1 filled in these gaps and added isolated accounts and PDF output. This article follows the current source and changelog. It describes the local exporter; private deployment changes and production verification are separate work.

Release update (3 November 2026): 1.11.2 is published, fixing Windows PDF browser cold-start retries. The commands below apply to the current release.



The demo runs offline against synthetic materials, deliberately retaining a missing attachment and an unauthorized Google link to show how omissions are reported.

Start with a useful command

After installing Study Kit and selecting your units:

monash export FIT2109 --sync --format both --to "./exports"


The destination is a folder, not a zip filename. --sync refreshes this unit’s Moodle content and Ed Lessons before packaging. It leaves Ed discussions out. Without it, export only reads the local cache. --dir writes a directory rather than a zip, and --open reveals the result in the file manager.

In 1.11.1 an interactive terminal opens a folder picker if --to is absent; --no-ask skips it. The starting location is the previous choice or the system Downloads folder, including a relocated Windows Downloads folder. The command prints the destination before work starts and progress while rendering and packing.

Collect first, package second

There are three stages:

Moodle / Ed / course-linked Google files
                 |
         sync and normalize
                 |
     local files + SQLite metadata
                 |
  export.Plan: entries + missing + statistics
                 |
       optional offline PDF rendering
                 |
    zip or directory, including an index


The code is split accordingly: syncer.py and moodle_content.py collect Moodle materials, the Ed modules collect Lessons, google_export.py handles linked Google files, export.py plans the package, and pdfrender.py prints its Markdown pages. Packaging does not need a live session unless the CLI was explicitly asked to sync first.

Moodle Page, Book and assignment bodies become Markdown. The Book parser uses Moodle’s print view, which does not count as viewing individual chapters. Visible rubrics and marking guides are teaching materials too; a student’s submissions, grades and private feedback are excluded. Moodle folders use a whole-folder download, retaining subdirectories and original filenames, with individual-file fallback when necessary.

Ed lesson pages contribute text, slides, embedded Ed-hosted files and question-only quiz pages. Images from Moodle and Ed are saved under assets/, deduplicated by content, and linked relatively. A failed image keeps its remote link and becomes an index entry. Older extensionless Ed images saved as .img are renamed from their detected content during sync, rather than remaining files a viewer cannot recognize.

The package has a unit root, Moodle/, Ed Lessons/ and an index. Original PDFs, notebooks, code and archives retain their formats. Generated bodies, link lists, quizzes and the index use the chosen output format.

A Google link needs its own permission

uv tool install --reinstall --refresh "monash-study-kit[gmail]"
monash google login
monash export FIT2109 --refresh-google --format both --to "./exports"


Keep any other extras you already use in that install command. The optional dependency happens to be named gmail; Drive authorization is separate. monash google login requests only drive.readonly and writes google-drive-token.json, independently of Gmail’s token. The scope can read all Drive files accessible to the account; the exporter uses course-linked files. It cannot edit them and grants no Gmail access.

Docs and Slides normally become PDF, Sheets XLSX, and ordinary Drive files keep their format. monash config google_docs_format docx changes Docs to DOCX. It does not change Slides or the exporter’s own Markdown pages. --refresh-google implies sync and re-exports linked Google files.

An API export can fail because of file size, a disabled API, administrator policy or sharing permissions. Where supported, the dedicated login browser’s Google session is tried as a fallback, with cookies held in memory. It does not bypass sharing permissions. Google Forms remain links with a reason. Logout revokes the Drive authorization before deleting its local token; failed revocation keeps the token so the user can retry.

PDF is another output, not another sync format

Since 1.11, pdf is the initial export default. --format md avoids PDF printing; both keeps editable Markdown alongside generated PDFs. Synced text and the MCP search index remain unchanged.

One isolated temporary Chrome, Edge or Brave process prints the package’s pages offline. Local images are embedded, raw HTML is escaped, and remote requests are blocked. Without a supported browser, export falls back to Markdown and says why in the index and terminal. Version 1.11.1 retries Windows temporary-profile cleanup so a browser helper briefly holding a file does not invalidate an already completed export.

The cache key covers printable HTML and embedded image contents. Replacing a local image therefore changes the key even if the Markdown is identical. Cached PDFs live under data/pdf-cache/; oldest entries are evicted above 500 MB. JSON output reports generated and cached PDF counts and the fallback reason. These are implementation limits, not performance measurements.

Account isolation belongs before imports

monash --profile exchange setup
monash --profile exchange google login
monash --profile exchange export FIT2109 --sync --to "./exports"
monash profile list


Paths are fixed when modules are imported. entry.py therefore chooses the profile before importing the CLI and service modules. Named profiles keep credentials, databases, materials and browser sessions under separate profiles/NAME directories. They force materials-only mode: no Gmail sync, attendance, Ed discussions or personal-calendar setup. They cannot configure remote serving, monash connect, or an independent data-home move.

Cleanup is deliberately a separate command from the default account: monash profile remove exchange. It revokes Google tokens before removing login sessions, keeps materials and databases unless --all is supplied, and preserves files if revocation fails. Ed API-token deletion remains a manual step.

Complete also means naming the gaps

The exporter records missing local files, unsynced Ed units, failed Google exports and remaining remote images. Notebook image references that are missing or differ only by case are reported too. A successful zip does not prove that every linked resource was downloadable. Folder refreshes are normally limited to once a week; refreshing Google is not a universal force-refresh switch.

The package excludes personal records and strips meeting-password parameters from links, but its contents are ordinary local files. They are not automatically public or safe to redistribute. Gmail is a separate optional feature: ordinary Gmail login requests gmail.modify, while --read-only requests gmail.readonly.

For this update, the local Study Kit suite completed with 663 passed and 10 skipped. Those tests cover synthetic export fixtures, Google errors, profiles and PDF behavior; they do not establish that every real course, Google account or Windows installation works. The bilingual export guide documents setup, options and retry steps. The practical check after exporting is still to open the index and inspect what was left out.

title: 导出整门课的课程资料
description: Study Kit 1.8 到 1.11.1 把 Moodle Page、Book、作业说明、Ed Lessons 和 Google 文件导出成一个本地资料包，并列出缺了什么
content:
上一篇 Ed 导出文章讲的是 lesson 文件夹和一键打包

但一门课还有别的东西：Moodle Page 里的作业要求、Book 的几个章节、评分标准、lesson 正文里的图片，以及仍然只是链接的 Google 文档

把磁盘上已有的 PDF 压缩起来，这些内容还是没带走

Study Kit 1.8 加了整课资料包，1.9 到 1.11.1 逐步补齐正文、图片、Google 文件、隔离账号和 PDF 输出

下面按当前源码和更新日志说明本地导出器的实现；私有部署改动和生产验证是另外的工作

发布更新（2026-11-03）： 1.11.2 已正式发布，修复 Windows PDF 浏览器冷启动重试；下文命令适用于当前版本



示例使用合成资料实际离线导出，保留一个缺失附件和未授权 Google 链接，展示索引如何报告遗漏

先看怎么用

装好 Study Kit、选好课程后：

monash export FIT2109 --sync --format both --to "./exports"


--to 是目标文件夹，不是 zip 文件名

--sync 先刷新这门课的 Moodle 和 Ed Lessons，不同步 Ed 讨论区；不加时只读本地缓存

--dir 输出文件夹，--open 在文件管理器里显示结果

1.11.1 起，交互终端不写 --to 会先弹目录选择框，--no-ask 跳过弹窗

默认上次选择的位置或系统下载目录，也支持 Windows 移动过的“下载”文件夹

同步前先告诉你存在哪，生成 PDF 和打包时显示进度

先采集，再打包

整个过程分三层：

Moodle / Ed / 课程链接的 Google 文件
                  |
              同步与规范化
                  |
         本地文件 + SQLite 元数据
                  |
    export.Plan：文件项 + 遗漏项 + 统计
                  |
           可选的离线 PDF 渲染
                  |
           zip 或目录，附带索引


对应源码中，syncer.py、moodle_content.py 收集 Moodle 内容，Ed 模块同步 Lessons，google_export.py 处理 Google 链接，export.py 生成打包计划，pdfrender.py 负责把 Markdown 页面打印成 PDF

只有 CLI 明确要求先同步时，打包前才需要在线会话

Moodle Page、Book 和作业正文存成 Markdown

Book 读打印视图，不计作逐章查看

学生可见的 rubric 和 marking guide 也是教学资料，但个人提交、成绩和反馈不进入资料包

文件夹优先整体下载，保留子目录和原文件名，失败再逐个获取

Ed Lessons 则提供正文、幻灯片、Ed 托管附件和只有题目的测验页

Moodle 与 Ed 图片存进 assets/，按内容去重，再改为相对引用

下载失败时保留远程地址，并写入索引

旧版本把无扩展名 Ed 图片存成 .img 的，同步时按实际内容修正扩展名，让图片查看器能够识别

包内按课号组织，下有 Moodle/、Ed Lessons/ 和索引

原有 PDF、notebook、代码和压缩包保留格式；生成的正文、链接列表、测验和索引则使用选定的格式

Google 链接需要单独授权

uv tool install --reinstall --refresh "monash-study-kit[gmail]"
monash google login
monash export FIT2109 --refresh-google --format both --to "./exports"


如果已经使用其他 extras，安装命令里也要保留

可选依赖虽然叫 gmail，Drive 授权却是独立的：monash google login 只申请 drive.readonly，保存在 google-drive-token.json，与 Gmail 令牌分离

该权限允许读取账号有权访问的全部 Drive 文件，导出器实际处理课程链接；它不能改文件，也不授予 Gmail 权限

Docs 和 Slides 默认 PDF，Sheets 是 XLSX，普通 Drive 文件保留原格式

monash config google_docs_format docx 只把 Docs 改成 DOCX，不影响 Slides 或导出器自己的 Markdown 正文

--refresh-google 隐含同步，并重新导出链接的 Google 文件

文件过大、API 未启用、管理员限制、未共享给当前账号，都可能导致 API 失败

支持时会尝试专用登录浏览器的 Google 会话，Cookie 只在内存中，不能绕过共享权限

Google Forms 保留链接和原因

退出授权先吊销再删本机令牌；吊销失败保留文件，让用户能继续重试

PDF 是输出格式，不是另一套同步

1.11 起初始默认输出 pdf；--format md 不打印 PDF，both 同时保留可编辑 Markdown

同步保存的文本和 MCP 搜索索引不变

每次导出使用一个独立的临时 Chrome、Edge 或 Brave 进程离线打印，嵌入已有本地图片、转义原始 HTML，并阻止远程请求

没有支持的浏览器就回退 Markdown，在终端和索引解释

1.11.1 会重试 Windows 临时 profile 清理，避免浏览器辅助进程短暂占用文件时，把已经完成的导出判为失败

缓存键包含打印 HTML 和嵌入图片内容，因此只替换图片、不改 Markdown，也会生成新的键

PDF 缓存在 data/pdf-cache/，超过 500 MB 时淘汰最旧项；JSON 报告生成数量、缓存命中数量和回退原因

这些是实现规则，不是性能测试数据

账号选择必须早于 import

monash --profile exchange setup
monash --profile exchange google login
monash --profile exchange export FIT2109 --sync --to "./exports"
monash profile list


模块 import 时就固定路径，所以 entry.py 必须先选账号，再加载 CLI 和服务模块

命名 profile 将凭据、数据库、课件和浏览器会话隔离在 profiles/NAME 下，强制只导课程资料：跳过 Gmail、考勤、Ed 讨论区和个人日历设置，也不能配置远程服务、monash connect 或独立移动资料根目录

清理从默认账号执行：monash profile remove exchange

先吊销 Google 令牌，再清登录会话；不加 --all 就保留课件和数据库，吊销失败则保留本机文件

Ed API 令牌仍需手动删除

完整还包括说清楚缺了什么

索引会列出本地文件缺失、Ed 课程未同步、Google 导出失败和剩余远程图片

notebook 引用的图片不存在、或者只是大小写不匹配，也要报告

zip 生成成功不代表每个链接都能下载；Moodle 文件夹通常最多每周刷新一次，刷新 Google 不是对所有资源强制刷新

资料包排除个人记录，并去掉链接里的会议密码参数，但导出后仍是普通本地文件，分享前要检查，不能因此视为可以公开转载

Gmail 是另一项可选功能：普通登录申请 gmail.modify，加 --read-only 才申请 gmail.readonly

本次本地 Study Kit 测试结果是 663 passed、10 skipped，覆盖合成资料、Google 错误、profile 和 PDF 行为，不代表每门真实课程、Google 账号和 Windows 环境都已经实测

双语导出指南列出了安装、参数和重试方式

真正导出后，仍应先打开索引，看清楚哪些内容没有带走

title: Zipping a unit's Ed materials in Study Kit
description: Study Kit can now zip a unit's Ed Lessons by week. Getting there meant renaming existing files, downloading attachments and fixing a deploy.
content:
Someone asked a simple question I hadn’t thought of. Ed Web has a button that downloads a whole unit’s Ed Lessons as one zip, sorted by week. Why doesn’t Study Kit have one, when it already syncs those files to your computer?

It did sync them. It just kept them in folders named after Ed’s numeric ids, like 39026/116285/201_Workshop 3 Slides.pdf, skipped files attached inside Ed pages, and had no way to hand you the lot. My private server version had the same gap, from the other side: the zip existed on its website, but Claude could not give it to you in a conversation.

This post is about closing that gap in three places: Study Kit, ed-digest (my server’s Ed sync), and the remote MCP server that connects them to claude.ai.

What it looks like now

$ monash ed export FIT2109 --module "Week 3"
已打包 FIT2109：3 节 lesson、5 个文件（0.0 MB）
  ~/Downloads/FIT2109 Ed Lessons (Week 3) 2026-11-01.zip


FIT2109 Ed Lessons/README.md
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/07 W3 Pre-Class/Links.md
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/07 W3 Pre-Class/02 Before class.md
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/08 W3 Workshop/01 Workshop 3 Slides.pdf
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/08 W3 Workshop/02 Workshop 3 Handout.pdf
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/09 W3 Applied Session/01 applied3-starter.zip
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/09 W3 Applied Session/01 Lab brief.md


That is a real run against synthetic course data; the CLI prints in Chinese because most of the people using it read Chinese. The same zip is one click on the local library page, and one sentence in an AI app.


  
    127.0.0.1:8766 · monash library
    
      
      
    
  
  The local library page with the new button. Moodle and Ed files for a unit now sit in one group. Screenshot of the real page, captured at 2x, with made-up course data.


Renaming files without downloading them again

Readable folders were the easy part to want and the fiddly part to ship. Everyone who upgrades already has a folder of PDFs under the old names. Downloading them all again would be slow and rude to Ed’s file server, so the sync looks up where each slide was stored last time and moves it:

def _move_old(old: str | None, new: str) -> None:
    if not old or old == new:
        return
    src, dest = FILES_DIR / old, FILES_DIR / new
    if src.is_file() and not dest.exists():
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        os.replace(src, dest)


The new path is <unit>/<NN module>/<NN lesson>/<NN title>. The numbers are needed. Without them, Finder sorts “Week 10” before “Week 2”, and modules come out in the order of their database ids rather than the order on Ed, so the module number comes from the position of its first lesson. Unit codes need care too: FIT3162/FIT3164 is one unit on Ed, and a slash is a folder separator, so it becomes FIT3162+FIT3164.

The same move also covers a lesson that gets renamed on Ed, and files of slides that disappear are deleted along with any folder they leave empty.

Attachments, and a stable id for something that has none

Starter code usually is not a PDF slide. It is a <file> element inside a text page. Those are now downloaded too, but only when the link points at Ed’s own file host, and only up to 200 MB each.

Every row in lesson_files is keyed by Ed’s slide id, and an attachment does not have one. I wanted to reuse the table, so every reader of it (the library, search, the lesson reader) would pick attachments up for free. The id is derived from the URL:

def attachment_id(url: str) -> int:
    return -int.from_bytes(hashlib.sha256(url.encode()).digest()[:7], "big") - 1


Negative, so it can never collide with a real slide; stable, so the next sync finds the file it saved last time; and tied to the URL, so when a teacher replaces the file, Ed issues a new URL, the id changes, the new file is downloaded and the old one is cleaned up. PDF slides follow the same rule: a changed file_url forces a fresh download instead of keeping the stale copy.

The zip is built from the database, not the disk

The export does not walk the folder. It reads modules, lessons and files from SQLite, works out the readable path again, and adds a README.md with each lesson’s progress and Ed link, a Links.md for reading pages, and a list of anything that failed to download. Two things fall out of that: a student who exports before their first sync on the new version still gets a properly named zip, and a missing file is reported instead of silently absent.

A bug the tests had hidden

While wiring the button into the library page I found that the page had never listed Ed files synced by Study Kit itself. The code checked whether a path sat under the Ed folder, but the database stores relative paths, so the check always failed. The existing test passed because it inserted an absolute path. The fix is one line, and test fixtures should be written the way production writes data. There is now a test with a relative path.

Adding a tool without growing every conversation

Every MCP tool’s name, description and schema is sent to the model in every conversation, used or not, so the project keeps a budget: a test fails if the catalog grows past a size, and another pins the original tools’ contract with a hash. export_ed_lessons fits in about 360 characters, and none of the old tools changed.

It is also the first Ed tool that writes something, a zip in your Downloads folder, so it is not marked read-only. That had a useful side effect: remote mode only exposes read-only tools, so a ChatGPT connected to someone’s self-hosted Study Kit never writes zips onto their server.

The server side

My own setup is different. ed-digest syncs Ed on a VPS and already builds a per-unit zip for its website. Rather than write a second packer, the remote MCP server loads ed-digest’s site.py and calls the same two functions, so the zip from Claude and the zip from the website cannot drift apart. It has to load it by path, because import site would quietly give you Python’s standard library module.

Claude cannot reach a file on my server, so the tool returns a link:

def download_sig(rel: str, exp: int) -> str:
    return hmac.new(_download_key(), f"{exp}:{rel}".encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()[:32]


The signature covers the path and the expiry, so changing either gives a 403, and the ed-export/ prefix only resolves to zips sitting directly in the export folder. Because one repository now depends on two functions in another, ed-digest has a contract test that pins their names and parameters. If someone renames them, ed-digest’s own CI fails, not a student’s request on a Sunday night.

ed-digest also picked up the improvements from Study Kit: numbered weeks in Ed’s order and attachments in the zip.

The server was not running what I thought

The plan was “pull and restart”. Before that I checked the service, and the live connector was not running from the repository at all. A systemd drop-in pointed it at a release snapshot, releases/student-20261031-r2, with its own virtualenv. The repository on disk was four pull requests behind.

So the deploy followed the snapshot pattern instead:


  Hash every file in the live snapshot and compare with git. The running code matched main before my change exactly, so the release would differ from production by this work only.
  Record the old symlink target, the drop-in and pip freeze for rollback.
  Unpack the merged commit into a new release, install the new core into a throwaway virtualenv on the server and run the whole suite there: 150 passed.
  Upgrade the live environment, switch the symlink, update the build SHA, restart.
  Call the tool with the service’s own environment, then download the signed link from outside: 200 with the zip, and 403 with a forged signature.


Then I updated the repository copy too, which runs the timers and the SSH version of the server. The only package that changed in that environment was the core, which I confirmed by diffing pip freeze before and after.

Follow-up: the whole-course exporter adds Moodle bodies, Google files, PDFs and isolated accounts.

title: Study Kit 打包整门课的 Ed 课件
description: Study Kit 现在能把一门课的 Ed 课件按周打包，过程中改了已有文件的命名、补下了附件，还修了一次部署问题
content:
这个问题很简单，我之前没想到

Ed Web 有个按钮，能把一门课的 Ed Lessons 按周打成一个 zip 下载

Study Kit 明明已经把这些文件同步到你电脑上了，为什么没有？

文件确实同步了，只是放在按 Ed 数字 id 命名的文件夹里，比如 39026/116285/201_Workshop 3 Slides.pdf；Ed 正文页里附的文件不会下载；也没有办法把整门课一次交给你

我服务器上的私人版本缺的是另一头：网站上有 zip，但 Claude 在对话里给不了你

这篇讲怎么在三个地方把它补上：Study Kit、ed-digest（我服务器上的 Ed 同步），以及把它们接到 claude.ai 的远程 MCP 服务器

现在是什么样

$ monash ed export FIT2109 --module "Week 3"
已打包 FIT2109：3 节 lesson、5 个文件（0.0 MB）
  ~/Downloads/FIT2109 Ed Lessons (Week 3) 2026-11-01.zip


FIT2109 Ed Lessons/README.md
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/07 W3 Pre-Class/Links.md
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/07 W3 Pre-Class/02 Before class.md
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/08 W3 Workshop/01 Workshop 3 Slides.pdf
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/08 W3 Workshop/02 Workshop 3 Handout.pdf
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/09 W3 Applied Session/01 applied3-starter.zip
FIT2109 Ed Lessons/03 Week 3 - Editor-Modern IDE/09 W3 Applied Session/01 Lab brief.md


这是用编造的课程数据真实跑出来的结果

同样的 zip，在本机课件页上点一下就有，在 AI 软件里说一句也行


  
    127.0.0.1:8766 · monash library
    
      

    
  
加了按钮的本机课件页

同一门课的 Moodle 和 Ed 文件现在放在同一组

真实页面的 2 倍截图，课程数据是编的




改名，但不重新下载

文件夹名好读，是最容易想要、也最麻烦落地的部分

每个升级的人手里都已经有一堆按旧名字存的 PDF

全部重新下载又慢，又给 Ed 的文件服务器添负担

所以同步时先查这一页上次存在哪，直接挪过去：

def _move_old(old: str | None, new: str) -> None:
    if not old or old == new:
        return
    src, dest = FILES_DIR / old, FILES_DIR / new
    if src.is_file() and not dest.exists():
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        os.replace(src, dest)


新路径是 课号/NN 模块/NN lesson/NN 标题

前面的编号比看上去重要：不加的话，访达会把 Week 10 排在 Week 2 前面；模块按数据库 id 排，也不一定是 Ed 上的顺序

所以模块编号取它第一节 lesson 在 Ed 上的位置

课号也要处理：FIT3162/FIT3164 在 Ed 上是一门课，但斜杠是路径分隔符，所以变成 FIT3162+FIT3164

Ed 上给 lesson 改了名，也走同一套挪动

页删了，本地文件跟着删，删空的文件夹也一起清掉

附件，以及给没有 id 的东西一个稳定的 id

starter code 通常不是一页 PDF，而是文字页里的一个 <file>

现在这些也会下载，但只限 Ed 自己的文件服务器上的链接，单个不超过 200 MB

lesson_files 每一行都以 Ed 的 slide id 为键，附件没有这个 id

我想沿用这张表，这样课件页、全文搜索、lesson 阅读器这些读它的地方就都自动认得附件

所以 id 由 URL 算出来：

def attachment_id(url: str) -> int:
    return -int.from_bytes(hashlib.sha256(url.encode()).digest()[:7], "big") - 1


负数，永远不会和真的 slide 撞；固定，下次同步能找到上次存的文件；和 URL 绑在一起，老师换了文件，Ed 会给一个新 URL，id 随之改变，新文件被下载，旧的被清掉

PDF 页也用同样的规则：file_url 变了就重新下载，不再留着旧版本

zip 从数据库生成，不从磁盘

打包不去遍历文件夹，而是从 SQLite 读模块、lesson 和文件，重新算出好读的路径，再写一个 README.md（每节的进度和 Ed 链接、没下载到的文件），阅读网页写进 Links.md

这样有两个好处：升级后还没同步就导出，zip 里的名字也是对的；文件缺了会写出来，而不是悄悄不见

一个被测试掩盖的 bug

把按钮接进课件页时，我发现这个页面其实从来没列出过 Study Kit 自己同步的 Ed 文件

代码判断路径是否在 Ed 文件夹里，可数据库存的是相对路径，所以永远判断失败

原来的测试能过，是因为它插进去的是绝对路径

修起来只要一行，测试数据应该按生产环境写数据的方式来造

现在多了一个用相对路径的测试

加一个工具，但不让每次对话都变长

每个 MCP 工具的名字、说明和参数，每次对话都会整份发给模型，用不用都算

所以项目里有预算：工具清单超过一定大小测试就失败，原有工具的契约还用哈希钉住

export_ed_lessons 大约 360 个字符，老工具一个字没改

它也是第一个会写东西的 Ed 工具（往你的“下载”文件夹写一个 zip），所以没有标成只读

这带来一个好处：远程模式只提供只读工具，所以连到别人自建 Study Kit 的 ChatGPT，永远不会往对方服务器上写 zip

服务器那边

我自己的部署不一样

ed-digest 在 VPS 上同步 Ed，本来就会给网站的每门课打一个 zip

与其再写一个打包器，远程 MCP 服务器直接加载 ed-digest 的 site.py，调用同样的两个函数，这样 Claude 给的 zip 和网站上的 zip 不可能对不上

它必须按文件路径加载，因为 import site 会悄悄拿到 Python 标准库里的 site

Claude 拿不到我服务器上的文件，所以工具返回一个链接：

def download_sig(rel: str, exp: int) -> str:
    return hmac.new(_download_key(), f"{exp}:{rel}".encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()[:32]


签名同时覆盖路径和过期时间，改哪个都是 403；ed-export/ 前缀只能解析到导出文件夹里直接放着的 zip

现在一个仓库依赖另一个仓库的两个函数，所以 ed-digest 加了契约测试，钉住它们的名字和参数

谁改了名字，失败的是 ed-digest 自己的 CI，而不是某个同学周日晚上的一次请求

ed-digest 也顺带吃到了 Study Kit 的改进：周文件夹按 Ed 上的顺序编号，zip 里有附件

服务器跑的不是我以为的那份

原计划是拉代码、重启

动手前我看了一眼服务配置，线上的连接器根本不是从仓库跑的：一个 systemd drop-in 把它指向了一个发布快照 releases/student-20261031-r2，用的是另一个 virtualenv

磁盘上的仓库落后了四个 PR

所以部署改成按快照的方式来：


  把线上快照里每个文件算哈希，和 git 对比，运行中的代码和我改动之前的 main 完全一致，所以新版本和线上的差别只有这次的工作
  记下旧的软链接目标、drop-in 和 pip freeze，用来回滚
  把合并后的提交解到新的 release 目录，在服务器上用一个临时 virtualenv 装新的核心包，跑完整测试：150 个通过
  升级线上环境，切换软链接，更新构建 SHA，重启
  用服务自己的环境调用一次工具，再从外网下载签名链接：正常的拿到 zip（200），伪造签名的返回 403


之后我也更新了仓库那一份，它跑定时任务和 SSH 版的服务器

这个环境里唯一变化的包是核心包，我用前后两次 pip freeze 的差异确认过

几点体会


  改用户文件的名字时，挪已有的，重新下载既耽误用户，也消耗上游服务器的带宽
  没有 id 的东西也需要稳定的 id，从“内容变了它就变”的东西里推出来
  导出要从唯一可信的数据源生成，而不是磁盘上碰巧有什么
  测试数据要像生产数据，不然测试会因为错误的理由通过
  一个仓库调用另一个仓库时，在被调用的那边钉住契约
  部署之前，先确认服务器实际在跑什么


后续：整课导出系统补上了 Moodle 正文、Google 文件、PDF 与隔离账号

title: Server alerts that only report changes
description: The Linux checks track state, so they alert on a new problem and on recovery instead of every run, and automatic fixes have limits.
content:
With several Linux machines, the first monitor most people write is a scheduled SSH check that looks at disks and containers and sends a message when something is wrong.

That works at first. But a failure that lasts for hours sends the same message on every run, and dozens of identical alerts make a new problem easy to miss.

Keeping state between checks

Edge Fleet Ops Automation is a cleaned up rebuild of tools I used for Linux edge nodes. The parts worth reusing are node discovery, health checks, saved state and deduplicated alerts.

The first time a disk goes over the threshold, I get an alert. The next ten checks don’t repeat it. When it recovers, I get one more message. Requiring a few failed checks in a row also avoids alerts from short network drops.

Limits on automatic fixes

Deleting files, restarting services and freeing disk space can be automated, but a wrong action can make things worse. I run these in dry run mode first, keep each one narrow, and decide case by case which ones can run unattended.

The public repository doesn’t mean these tools run on my J1900 or N1 boxes now. It records the approach I want to reuse when I set up their monitoring again.

title: 只在状态变化时发的服务器告警
description: Linux 巡检会记录状态，只在出新问题和恢复时提醒，自动修复也有次数限制
content:
有几台 Linux 机器时，最先想到的监控通常是定时 SSH 上去看看磁盘和容器，有问题就发消息

一开始这样够用，但一个故障持续几个小时，每次检查都会再发一遍，几十条一样的告警里，新的问题反而容易被漏掉

记录每次检查的状态

Edge Fleet Ops Automation 是我以前给 Linux 边缘节点用的工具，脱敏后重新整理过，值得再用的是节点发现、健康检查、保存状态和告警去重

磁盘第一次超过阈值时发一条，后面十次检查不再重复，恢复时再发一条，要求连续几次失败才告警，也能避免网络短暂断开时误报

自动修复要有限制

删文件、重启服务、清磁盘空间都可以自动做，但做错了可能让问题更严重，我会先用 dry run 跑，每个操作范围尽量小，再逐个决定哪些可以无人值守

公开仓库不代表这些工具现在跑在我的 J1900 或 N1 上，它记录的是我重新搭监控时想沿用的做法

title: SecureView concurrency testing
description: Connection pool exhaustion and deadlocks only showed up once the file sharing app had many users at the same time.
content:
SecureView was our four-person final year project, a file sharing app where files are encrypted in the browser. My parts included testing, CI, deployment and some of the security features. In a one-person demo you see encryption, upload, sharing and decryption. Later I spent more time on database connections, concurrent requests and what happens after a failure.

Upload failures that had nothing to do with encryption

A load test with 100 users found a connection pool problem. Many uploads failed before we found and fixed it. The results are in the project README, and this post doesn’t add new benchmark numbers.

We also hit MySQL deadlocks. These came from transaction boundaries and the order rows were locked in. A single upload never runs into them.

A test for each fix

After fixing a concurrency bug I want a test that reproduces it, since a few manual retries that happen to pass don’t prove much. The MySQL tests, browser tests and fault injection cases are there to catch the same bugs again.

To understand a deadlock you need to know which statements lock which rows, how retries work and whether a write finished. The error message alone doesn’t tell you that.

The SecureView repository has the earlier measurements and environment notes. This post looks back at the testing and doesn’t make claims about the current deployment.

title: SecureView 的并发测试
description: 连接池耗尽和死锁，是文件分享系统有多人同时使用后才出现的问题
content:
SecureView 是我们四个人的毕业设计，一个在浏览器里加密文件的文件分享系统，我负责测试、CI、部署和一部分安全功能

一个人演示时看到的是加密、上传、分享和解密，后来我花了更多时间在数据库连接、并发请求和失败之后的处理上

和加密无关的上传失败

100 个用户的压测发现了连接池的问题，修好之前有很多上传失败，测试结果写在项目 README 里，这篇不再给新的数据

我们还遇到过 MySQL 死锁，原因在事务边界和锁行的顺序，只上传一个文件时根本碰不到

每个修复都配一个测试

修好一个并发问题后，我会写一个能重现它的测试，手动重试几次刚好成功说明不了什么，MySQL 测试、浏览器测试和故障注入就是用来防止同样的问题再出现

要弄清一次死锁，需要知道哪些语句锁了哪些行、重试怎么做、写入到底有没有完成，光看报错信息是不够的

以前的测试数据和环境说明在 SecureView 仓库里，这篇只是回顾测试过程，不代表现在部署的性能

title: Why I built a degree planner for Monash
description: Checking prerequisites, campuses and teaching periods against the Handbook, with a source for each result.
content:
When I plan a Monash degree, typing in unit codes is quick. What takes time is checking whether each unit runs at my campus, whether it is offered in the semester I picked, and whether I can finish its prerequisites before then.

A spreadsheet can hold a plan but it doesn’t check any of that. That is one of the reasons I built Monash Hub.

The plan stays in the browser

Students drag units between semesters, undo changes and export the plan. When they ask for a check, the units in the plan are sent to an API that uses Handbook data. The server doesn’t keep a copy of the plan.

“Not found” and “not allowed” are treated differently. If the local data has no record of a unit for a year, that doesn’t mean the unit was cancelled. A prerequisite warning comes with the reason and a link to the Handbook entry.

Warnings, not approvals

The tool can’t approve a prerequisite exemption, credit transfer or graduation. It points out possible problems early and links to the Handbook page, so the student knows what to ask the faculty.

The source has the plan model and the checks. Comparing different Handbook years still needs work, because newer rules shouldn’t replace the ones that applied when a student started.

title: 我为什么做 Monash 选课规划工具
description: 按 Handbook 检查先修课、校区和开课学期，每个结果都附上来源
content:
规划 Monash 的课程时，输入课号很快，花时间的是检查每门课在不在自己校区开、选的学期有没有开、先修课能不能在之前修完

表格可以记规划，但不会帮你检查这些，这是我做 Monash Hub 的原因之一

规划留在浏览器里

可以把课拖到不同学期、撤销修改、导出规划，需要检查时，规划里的课会发给一个用 Handbook 数据的接口，服务器不保存规划

“没找到”和“不允许”分开处理，本地数据里某一年没有这门课，不代表这门课停开了，先修课的提醒会写明原因，并附上 Handbook 的链接

只是提醒，不是批准

这个工具不能批准先修课豁免、学分转换或者毕业审核，它只是提前指出可能的问题，附上 Handbook 页面，让同学知道该去问学院什么

规划模型和检查规则在源码里，不同 Handbook 年份的对比还需要改进，学生入学时适用的规则不应该被新规则覆盖

title: How this blog is built and served
description: Posts are built with Jekyll, served from my VPS, and GitHub Pages stays up as a mirror.
content:
The blog is built with Jekyll. It handles posts, layouts, the feed and the sitemap, and each Chinese post shares a ref with its English version so readers can switch language. I thought about turning it into a web app with a database, but the site mostly turns Markdown into pages, so I kept Jekyll and only redid the home page.

Where it is built and where it is served

The source is in waldo0926.github.io. GitHub Actions builds the site into a separate site branch, and my VPS pulls that branch on a schedule and serves blog.secureview.tech. The VPS only serves static files and doesn’t run Jekyll.

The GitHub Pages address still works as a mirror. There is no automatic failover between the two.

Checks on each PR

A broken template can take down a whole page, so every PR builds the site and checks that each post has its link preview image.

Links are the other thing that breaks. The English and Chinese versions of a post link to each other, and so do the project pages. A change to the domain or the navigation can break these without any code change.

The repository README has the current setup. This post describes how it works now and may go out of date if I change the deployment.

title: 这个博客怎么构建和部署
description: 文章用 Jekyll 构建，主站放在我的 VPS 上，GitHub Pages 作为镜像
content:
博客用 Jekyll 生成，文章、布局、RSS 和 sitemap 它都能处理，中英文两篇用同一个 ref 互相链接，读者可以切换语言

我考虑过改成带数据库的网站，但这个站主要就是把 Markdown 变成网页，所以还是用 Jekyll，只重做了首页

在哪构建，在哪部署

源码在 waldo0926.github.io，GitHub Actions 把网站构建到单独的 site 分支，我的 VPS 定时拉这个分支，提供 blog.secureview.tech

VPS 上只放静态文件，不跑 Jekyll

GitHub Pages 的地址还能打开，当作镜像，两边之间没有自动切换

每个 PR 都会检查

模板写错可能让整个页面打不开，所以每个 PR 都会构建一次网站，并检查每篇文章有没有分享预览图

另一个容易出问题的是链接，中英文文章要互相链接，项目页面也一样，改域名或导航时，代码没动这些链接也可能断掉

现在的做法写在仓库 README 里，以后部署方式改了，这篇可能就不准了

title: String algorithms code I kept after the course
description: Z matching, BWT search, Ukkonen suffix trees and Rabin Karp rebuilt as a standalone repo, with their limitations written down.
content:
When I went back to my algorithms coursework, I didn’t want to put the old assignment folder on GitHub as it was. The code might still run, but without notes on the design, complexity and edge cases it wouldn’t be much use to anyone, including me a year later.

I moved four parts into a separate Python repository: exact matching with the Z algorithm, approximate matching with BWT, Ukkonen suffix trees with LCP extraction, and Rabin Karp with Miller Rabin prime generation.

Limitations

It isn’t a production search engine. The BWT example uses a simple suffix array builder on purpose, and the Z matcher here has an O(m²) preprocessing step for shifts. Calling either a fast text search would hide that cost.

For Ukkonen’s suffix tree, the bugs I kept hunting were in the active point, suffix links and skip/count. The code is written so those steps can be followed one at a time.

Testing

For BWT approximate matching, the tests cover substitution, insertion, deletion and transposition separately. The LCP array is compared against a naive version on small inputs. Rabin Karp checks each candidate against the text, since equal hashes don’t prove a match.

There are runnable examples and pytest tests. Assignment sheets, marking material and other course resources are not included.

More notes are in ALGORITHMS.md. Before using any of this for indexing at scale, I’d benchmark the real workload and replace the simple construction steps.

title: 字符串算法课结束后留下的代码
description: 把 Z 匹配、BWT、Ukkonen 后缀树和 Rabin Karp 整理成单独的仓库，并写明各自的限制
content:
回头整理算法课的代码时，我不想把以前的作业文件夹原样放上 GitHub，代码也许还能跑，但没有设计、复杂度和边界情况的说明，别人看不懂，一年后的我也一样

我把四部分整理成一个单独的 Python 仓库：Z 算法精确匹配、基于 BWT 的近似匹配、Ukkonen 后缀树和 LCP 提取，以及用 Miller Rabin 生成素数的 Rabin Karp

限制

它不是生产用的搜索引擎，BWT 的例子故意用了简单的后缀数组构建方法，这里的 Z 匹配在计算位移时有一步 O(m²) 的预处理，直接叫它们“快速文本搜索”会把这些开销藏起来

Ukkonen 后缀树里，我反复排查的问题都在 active point、suffix link 和 skip/count 上，代码写成可以一步一步跟着看的样子

测试

BWT 近似匹配的测试把替换、插入、删除和换位分开测，LCP 数组在小输入上和朴素算法对比，Rabin Karp 会拿原文核对每个候选，哈希相同不代表真的匹配

仓库里有能运行的例子和 pytest 测试，不包含作业题目、评分材料和其他课程资料

更多说明在 ALGORITHMS.md，真要拿来做大规模索引的话，我会先按实际数据测一下性能，再把简单的构建步骤换掉

title: What runs on my two J1900 boxes and the N1
description: Two J1900 boxes, a Debian N1 and a VPS, and how I decide what stays online and what can be wiped.
content:
I got two old J1900 machines working again. I also have an N1 box running Debian, and a VPS that hosts my public services. Before deciding what else to run on them, I want to know what I’d lose if one of them stopped working.

Not everything runs at home

The public sites run on the VPS, which already has HTTPS, automatic deploys and monitoring. Copying all of that to home machines doesn’t help much. The home IP changes, and power cuts, disk failures and router restarts are harder to deal with.

For now the larger J1900 is meant as a backup or standby, the other J1900 is for experiments, and the N1 is a small Debian test node. These are plans and nothing fails over automatically yet. Some of the machines can just stay off.

Writing down the restore steps

I want to write down what happens if the VPS or one of the disks fails:


  Which data exists in only one place?
  Can I restore a database and its files on a clean machine?
  How do I SSH in when the home IP changes?
  Which jobs need a schedule and which only run when I start them?
  Does an alert report a new failure, or the same one all day?


Installing Debian doesn’t answer any of these.

Older projects

My homelab network automation and edge fleet operations repositories are cleaned up rebuilds of earlier tools and don’t describe what runs on these machines now.

Some ideas from them I want to reuse: keeping alert state, checking a few times before acting, limiting what automation can do, and running in dry run mode by default. I’ll write about a real restore once I’ve done one.

title: 两台 J1900 和一台 N1 上跑什么
description: 两台 J1900、一台 Debian N1 和一台 VPS，哪些服务一直开着，哪些可以随时重装
content:
我把两台旧的 J1900 重新弄好了，另外还有一台装 Debian 的 N1，以及放公开服务的 VPS

在决定上面再跑什么之前，我想先弄清楚其中一台坏了会丢掉什么

不是所有东西都放在家里

公开的网站都在 VPS 上，HTTPS、自动部署和监控都已经有了，在家里再复制一套用处不大，家里的公网 IP 会变，停电、硬盘坏、路由器重启也更难处理

目前的打算是大一点的 J1900 做备份或备用机，另一台 J1900 用来做实验，N1 当一个小的 Debian 测试节点，这些只是计划，现在还没有自动切换，有的机器平时可以直接关着

把恢复步骤写下来

我想先写清楚 VPS 或某块硬盘坏了以后会怎样：


  哪些数据只有一份
  能不能在一台新机器上恢复数据库和对应的文件
  家里 IP 变了以后怎么 SSH 进去
  哪些任务要定时跑，哪些只在需要时手动跑
  告警是报告新的故障，还是一整天重复同一句话


装好 Debian 并不能回答这些问题

以前的项目

我以前写过 iKuai 网络自动化和 Linux 节点巡检，公开的仓库是脱敏后重新整理的版本，不代表现在这几台机器上跑着这些工具

里面有些做法我想继续用：记录告警状态、连续检查几次再处理、限制自动操作的范围、默认先 dry run，等真正做完一次恢复演练，再单独写结果

title: Study Kit 1.5.0: school mail and attendance
description: Study Kit can optionally read school mail and attendance. Actions that change something show a preview and only run after you confirm.
content:
Monash Study Kit used to read only Moodle and Ed. I had been using mail and attendance on my private deployment for a while, and 1.5.0, released on 31 October, brings them into the public version. Both are optional; nothing changes until you connect them.

The big difference from earlier releases is that it can now change things for the first time. Drafting mail, sending a draft, archiving and checking in to a class cannot be taken back if they go wrong. So this post is mostly about how those actions are kept in check, plus a few trade-offs I made so that students would actually use it.

Anything that changes something takes two steps

The AI cannot run a write in one step. It first calls a prepare tool and gets the full preview: recipients, Bcc, body and attachments, the label change, or the class and the code. The preview is stored as a ticket together with its SHA-256:

body = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
digest = hashlib.sha256(body.encode()).hexdigest()


To run it, the AI has to send the ticket ID, that hash and user_confirmed=true. The server’s instructions tell it to show the preview as it is and never confirm on the user’s behalf. A ticket expires after 10 minutes and works once. It is marked as executing before Gmail is contacted, so two clicks at the same time cannot send two emails. Before a draft is sent, its content is checked again, and a draft that changed after the preview is refused.

Failures come in two kinds. If a check fails before anything is sent, the ticket is marked rejected and you know nothing went out. If the request itself fails, it is marked unknown and is never retried by itself; you look at the mailbox first. Check-in is only prepared when you say you actually attended, and never for a class that has not started or is already done.

At first I left these writes off until the user turned them on in the settings. That felt broken in practice: a student logs in, asks the AI to archive a message, and the AI says it cannot. What actually protects the student is the two-step flow, not a switch. So in 1.5.0 they are on after login, and the switches stay for anyone who wants them off. The decision is written down in ADR 0004. Moodle and Ed are still read-only.

Each remote app picks what it gets

Remote mode in 1.4.0 had a single monash scope, so until now the remote server simply refused mail and attendance. Opening them up directly would have let a ChatGPT you paired last week read your whole mailbox without you knowing.

Now the pairing page shows a checkbox for each part the server owner has turned on: read-only ones start ticked, actions start unticked. The choice is stored with the authorization code and the tokens and survives refresh. Every call intersects it with the server’s current settings, so turning something off on the server takes it away from every app at once. Tokens from before 1.5.0 were set to monash when the database was upgraded, so old apps gain nothing. Tickets and background jobs belong to one client, so one app cannot run an action another app prepared.

Attendance without a browser

The attendance portal is an ASP.NET page where you switch days with a #daySel menu. My Chrome extension has always opened the page, switched to the day and run a JavaScript parser. Doing that in the background meant starting a headless browser and switching day by day, which is heavy for something that runs several times a day.

Switching days did not seem to load anything new; it only showed the matching dayPanel_<date> block. So every day was probably already in the HTML. I wrote a Python version of the parser that only looks inside that day’s block, and fetched the page once with the cookies saved at login.

A guess is not enough to ship, so there are two layers of comparison. In the tests, several differently structured pages go through the original JavaScript in a real browser and through the Python version, and the rows must match field by field, including the label text. There is also monash attendance probe, which reads the real portal both ways and prints only counts and whether they match, never course content. On the Malaysia campus portal, all 15 days it offers matched, and the page is 5 KB. So the fast read is on by default, and it falls back to the browser whenever the page looks different.

The first probe on my Mac failed with CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED. The portal most likely does not send its intermediate certificate; Chrome fetches it by itself, Python does not. The fix was truststore, which makes Python use the operating system’s verifier, and macOS fills in the missing certificate the same way Chrome does. Verification stays on the whole time.

When to read changed too. Instead of every hour, reads follow the timetable: weekday mornings at 8, and 15 minutes after each class you have not checked in to. Nothing runs at night, at weekends or for classes already done. I do not know yet how long the portal login lasts, so the program records each login, each successful read and the first expiry, and I will decide on a keepalive once there is data.

No terminal for students

Once it worked, there was another problem. Connecting Gmail meant creating a Google Cloud project, enabling the API, downloading a JSON file and typing a command. For most students that is so much work that Claude’s built-in Gmail connector is simply easier.

I did two things. First, the package now includes a desktop app client made just for the public version. Google designs these files to ship with the program; it only tells Google which app is asking and cannot read anyone’s mail. GitHub’s push protection still flagged it and I had to allow it by hand. The cost is the “this app isn’t verified” warning, and a limit of 100 users for an app Google has not reviewed, which is fine for a group of friends.

Second, a new tool, start_school_service_setup. A student says “connect my school email” in their AI app, and it installs the missing packages into the running install, opens the sign-in window and leaves only the sign-in to them. When it is done it tells the AI app to refresh its tool list. The tool costs about 145 tokens per conversation, so it hides itself once both parts are connected. The parameters of the original 17 tools are pinned by a hash in the tests, and none of them changed.

title: Study Kit 1.5.0：学校邮箱和考勤
description: Study Kit 可以选择接上学校邮箱和考勤，会改动内容的操作先给你看预览，确认后才执行
content:
Monash Study Kit 原来只读 Moodle 和 Ed

邮箱和考勤我一直在自己的私人部署上用，10 月 31 日发布的 1.5.0 把它们搬进了公开版

两部分都是可选的，接上之前什么都不会多

这次和以前最大的不同是：它第一次能改东西了

起草邮件、发草稿、归档、签到，做错了都收不回来

所以这篇主要讲这些操作是怎么管住的，还有几处为了让同学用得下去做的取舍

会改东西的，都分两步

AI 不能一步就执行写操作

它先调用 prepare，拿到一份完整预览：收件人、密送、正文、附件，或者要改的标签，或者是哪节课、哪个签到码

这份预览连同它的 SHA-256 存成一张凭据：

body = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
digest = hashlib.sha256(body.encode()).hexdigest()


执行时要带上凭据编号、这个哈希，还要 user_confirmed=true

服务器给 AI 的说明里写着：预览要原样给用户看，不能替用户确认

凭据 10 分钟过期，只能用一次

执行前先把它标成“正在执行”再去联系 Gmail，所以同时点两次也不会发出两封

发送草稿前还会再核对一次草稿内容，预览之后被改过就拒绝

出错也分两种

执行前的检查没过，记成“已拒绝”，可以确定什么都没发出去；真正发请求时出错，记成“结果未知”，不会自动重试，要先去邮箱里看看到底发没发

签到只有你说自己实际到课了才会准备，而且不能给还没开始或已经签过的课提交

一开始我让这些写操作默认关着，要用户自己去设置里打开

后来发现这样很别扭：同学登录完问 AI“帮我把这封归档”，AI 说做不到，看起来像坏了

真正起保护作用的是上面那个两步流程，不是开关

所以 1.5.0 改成登录以后就打开，开关留着给不想要的人关

这个决定写进了 ADR 0004

Moodle 和 Ed 还是只读，没有变

远程的每个软件自己选

1.4.0 的远程模式只有一个 monash 权限，所以之前的版本干脆整组拒绝邮箱和考勤

直接放开的话，已经配对过的 ChatGPT 会在你不知道的情况下突然能读整个邮箱

现在配对页上，服务器开了的功能各有一个勾选框：只读的默认勾上，写操作默认不勾

勾了什么就存进授权码和令牌，刷新令牌时一起带过去

每次调用时，再和服务器当前的设置取一次交集，服务器上关掉某项，所有软件马上就用不了

1.5.0 之前配对的令牌在数据库升级时补的是 monash，所以旧软件不会多出任何权限

凭据和后台任务也按客户端分开，一个软件准备的操作，另一个软件执行不了

考勤不开浏览器

考勤门户是一个 ASP.NET 页面，日期用 #daySel 下拉框切换

我的 Chrome 插件一直是让浏览器打开页面、切到那天、再跑一段 JavaScript 解析

放到后台定时跑，每次都要起一个无头浏览器，一天一天地切，很重

我注意到切日期时页面并不会重新请求，只是把对应的 dayPanel_<日期> 显示出来

那么所有日期很可能本来就在 HTML 里

于是写了一个 Python 版的解析器，只在当天那个区块里找，用登录时保存的 cookie 直接请求一次页面

光凭猜不能就这么上线，所以做了两层对照

测试里用几种不同结构的页面，让浏览器跑原来的 JS、Python 跑新的解析，逐条比较，连显示文字都要一样

另外加了一个 monash attendance probe，在真实门户上把两种读法各跑一遍，只输出数量和对不对得上，不输出课程内容

在马来西亚校区的门户上，门户提供的 15 天全部一致，页面只有 5 KB

所以快速读取默认打开了，页面结构对不上时会自动退回浏览器

第一次在 Mac 上跑 probe 时报了 CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED

门户服务器大概没把中间证书发全，Chrome 会自己去补，Python 自带的校验不会

最后用 truststore 让 Python 走系统的证书校验，macOS 会像 Chrome 一样补上

校验一直是开着的，没有为了能跑通去关掉它

读的时间也换了思路

不按钟点每小时跑，而是按课表：工作日早上 8 点读一次，每节还没签到的课开始 15 分钟后再读一次

晚上、周末和已经签过的课都不跑

登录能维持多久还不知道，所以程序会记下每次登录、每次成功和第一次过期的时间，等有了数据再决定要不要续期

不让同学开终端

功能做完后有一个问题：接 Gmail 要自己去 Google Cloud 建项目、开 API、下载一个 JSON，再在终端里输命令

这对大多数同学来说太难了，难到不如直接用 Claude 自带的 Gmail 连接器

我做了两件事

第一，安装包里带了一个公开版专用的桌面应用客户端

按 Google 的设计，桌面应用的这个文件本来就随程序公开，它只告诉 Google 是哪个应用在请求授权，拿不到任何人的邮件；GitHub 的推送保护还是会拦一下，要手动放行

代价是授权页会显示“尚未验证此应用”，而且没审核的应用最多 100 个用户，对朋友圈子够用

第二，加了一个工具 start_school_service_setup

同学在 AI 里说“帮我接上学校邮箱”，它在后台把缺的组件装进现在的环境，然后在电脑上打开登录窗口，同学只要登录

接好以后通知 AI 软件刷新工具列表

这个工具每次对话多占约 145 个 token，所以两样都接好以后它会自己隐藏

原来 17 个工具的参数在测试里是用哈希锁住的，这次一个都没改

title: Study Kit 1.4.0: remote mode for ChatGPT
description: ChatGPT and Claude on the web can now connect to Study Kit. It is still for one person, with pairing codes, fixed callback addresses and read-only tools.
content:
Monash Study Kit syncs your own Moodle and Ed to your computer and lets an AI app search them over MCP. Claude Desktop and Claude Code start it as a local program and talk to it over stdio. ChatGPT and Claude on the web or phone cannot do that. They live on someone else’s server, so they need an HTTPS address to call.

Version 1.4.0 came out on 30 October with an optional monash remote mode for this. This post is about how it is locked down, because a URL on the internet that can read your Moodle is not something to get wrong.

One person, their own data

I already decided not to host Study Kit for everyone. That would mean keeping every student’s Moodle login and Ed token on my server, and one break in would expose all of them. The docs explain the same reason.

So remote mode is for the owner of the data only. You run it on your own server, or on your own laptop behind a free Cloudflare quick tunnel, and it serves your synced files to your own AI apps. Setup never starts it, and installing or updating the package does not open any port. Nothing listens until you run monash remote serve yourself.

The server also refuses to bind anywhere except loopback:
